name: Mahamaya Antibiotic Intelligence Lab — Classification, Spectrum & Stewardship
scientific_boundary: Educational classification and spectrum navigation only. “Gram-positive/Gram-negative/MRSA/Pseudomonas/ESBL/CRE” tags mean a class or agent is commonly considered in that spectrum context when susceptible; they do not predict a patient isolate. Culture/AST, local antibiogram, infection site, source control, severity, PK/PD, organ function, allergy, age/pregnancy and current guidelines must govern treatment.

classification_notes.gram_positive: Gram-positive organisms retain crystal violet because of a thick peptidoglycan layer. Clinically important groups include Staphylococcus, Streptococcus and Enterococcus; species and resistance phenotype matter.
classification_notes.gram_negative: Gram-negative organisms have an outer membrane containing lipopolysaccharide and often multiple permeability/efflux/beta-lactamase resistance mechanisms. Important groups include Enterobacterales and non-fermenters such as Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter.
classification_notes.aware: WHO AWaRe is a stewardship framework (Access, Watch, Reserve), not a susceptibility or “best drug” ranking. Current 2025 WHO classification should be verified for local stewardship use.
classification_notes.ast: EUCAST/FDA breakpoints and the local microbiology laboratory determine susceptible/intermediate/increased-exposure/resistant interpretation; class-level spectrum is not a substitute.
classification_notes.static_cidal: Bactericidal/bacteriostatic is a simplified learning classification; effect can vary with organism, concentration, growth phase, site and combination therapy.

classes.name: Natural penicillins
classes.spectrum_note: Classic narrow-spectrum beta-lactams; activity depends on organism and beta-lactamase production.

classes.name: Anti-staphylococcal penicillins
classes.spectrum_note: Designed for penicillinase-producing MSSA; not MRSA.

classes.name: Aminopenicillins
classes.spectrum_note: Broader than natural penicillins; beta-lactamase susceptibility limits many organisms.

classes.name: Antipseudomonal penicillins
classes.spectrum_note: Antipseudomonal activity is agent- and susceptibility-dependent; usually used with a beta-lactamase inhibitor in modern practice.

classes.name: Beta-lactam + beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations
classes.spectrum_note: Spectrum varies markedly by beta-lactam and inhibitor; resistant phenotypes require organism-specific guidance.

classes.name: First-generation cephalosporins
classes.spectrum_note: Strong Gram-positive activity with limited Enterobacterales coverage; no Enterococcus.

classes.name: Second-generation cephalosporins / cephamycins
classes.spectrum_note: Second-generation spectrum varies; cephamycins add anaerobic activity.

classes.name: Third-generation cephalosporins
classes.spectrum_note: Expanded Gram-negative activity; ceftazidime is antipseudomonal while oral agents differ substantially.

classes.name: Fourth/fifth-generation cephalosporins
classes.spectrum_note: Cefepime provides antipseudomonal coverage; anti-MRSA activity is specific to agents such as ceftaroline/ceftobiprole.

classes.name: Advanced cephalosporin + beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations
classes.mechanism: PBP inhibition plus advanced beta-lactamase inhibition
classes.spectrum_note: Designed for selected resistant Gram-negative phenotypes; exact enzyme spectrum differs by inhibitor.

classes.name: Siderophore cephalosporin
classes.mechanism: Iron-transport facilitated entry plus PBP inhibition
classes.spectrum_note: Reserve-oriented Gram-negative agent; susceptibility testing and current guidance are essential.

classes.name: Carbapenems
classes.mechanism: Broad beta-lactam PBP inhibition with stability to many beta-lactamases
classes.spectrum_note: Very broad beta-lactams; ertapenem lacks reliable Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter activity.

classes.name: Carbapenem + beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations
classes.mechanism: Carbapenem PBP inhibition plus inhibitor activity against selected carbapenemases
classes.spectrum_note: Specialist therapy for selected resistant Gram-negative infections; enzyme type and AST matter.

classes.name: Monobactams
classes.spectrum_note: Aerobic Gram-negative activity; lacks Gram-positive and anaerobic activity.

classes.name: Glycopeptide antibiotics
classes.mechanism: Binds D-Ala-D-Ala and blocks peptidoglycan assembly
classes.spectrum_note: Gram-positive only; oral vancomycin acts locally in the gut for C. difficile.

classes.name: Lipoglycopeptides
classes.mechanism: Glycopeptide cell-wall inhibition plus membrane effects
classes.spectrum_note: Long-acting Gram-positive agents; indications and Enterococcus activity vary by agent.

classes.name: Cyclic lipopeptide
classes.spectrum_note: Daptomycin is not used for pneumonia because pulmonary surfactant inactivates activity.

classes.name: Macrolides
classes.spectrum_note: Useful atypical/respiratory coverage; pneumococcal/macrolide resistance is common in many settings.

classes.name: Tetracyclines
classes.spectrum_note: Broad intracellular/atypical and selected community Gram-positive activity; susceptibility varies.

classes.name: Glycylcycline / newer tetracycline derivatives
classes.mechanism: 30S inhibition with structural modifications that overcome selected resistance mechanisms
classes.spectrum_note: Broad agents with important exclusions; tigecycline/eravacycline do not cover Pseudomonas.

classes.name: Aminoglycosides
classes.mechanism: Irreversible 30S binding causes misreading and bactericidal protein-synthesis disruption
classes.spectrum_note: Concentration-dependent aerobic Gram-negative activity; no anaerobic activity; renal/ototoxicity monitoring is important.

classes.name: Fluoroquinolones
classes.mechanism: Inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
classes.spectrum_note: Spectrum differs by agent; resistance and safety warnings require stewardship.

classes.name: Folate-pathway inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Sequential folate-pathway inhibition (when trimethoprim + sulfonamide combined)
classes.spectrum_note: Co-trimoxazole has useful community MRSA and Stenotrophomonas activity when susceptible.

classes.name: Lincosamides
classes.spectrum_note: Covers many Gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm; C. difficile risk is important.

classes.name: Oxazolidinones
classes.mechanism: Blocks formation of the 50S initiation complex
classes.spectrum_note: Potent resistant Gram-positive activity; hematologic/serotonergic/neuropathy monitoring is duration-dependent.

classes.name: Streptogramins
classes.spectrum_note: Specialist Gram-positive therapy; VRE activity mainly relates to E. faecium, not E. faecalis.

classes.name: Phenicols
classes.spectrum_note: Broad historical agent limited by serious hematologic toxicity and safer alternatives.

classes.name: Systemic rifamycins
classes.spectrum_note: Resistance develops rapidly with monotherapy for many organisms; major drug interactions occur via enzyme induction.

classes.name: Polymyxins
classes.mechanism: Disrupts Gram-negative outer/cytoplasmic membranes via LPS binding
classes.spectrum_note: Last-line/reserve Gram-negative agents with nephro/neurotoxicity; intrinsic resistance occurs in several species.

classes.name: Nitroimidazoles
classes.mechanism: Reduced metabolites damage DNA in anaerobic organisms
classes.spectrum_note: Strong anaerobic activity below diaphragm; no meaningful aerobic bacterial activity.

classes.name: Urinary-focused antibacterials
classes.mechanism: Mechanism varies; high urinary exposure is central to use
classes.target: Urinary tract / bacterial enzymes or cell processes
classes.spectrum_note: Lower-UTI focused agents; tissue penetration and renal-function limits differ by drug.

classes.name: Pleuromutilins
classes.spectrum_note: Systemic lefamulin is respiratory-focused; retapamulin is topical.

classes.name: C. difficile-focused macrocyclic antibiotic
classes.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase at a distinct site
classes.spectrum_note: Fidaxomicin has minimal systemic absorption and is focused on C. difficile infection.

classes.name: Topical/local antibacterials
classes.mechanism: Local antibacterial mechanisms vary by agent
classes.spectrum_note: Local-use agents; avoid treating deep/systemic infection with topical therapy alone.

classes.name: Aminocyclitol antibacterial
classes.spectrum_note: Legacy/region-dependent gonococcal option where available; current STI guidance should be checked.

classes.name: Amidinopenicillins (mecillinam / pivmecillinam)
classes.spectrum_note: Urinary Enterobacterales-focused beta-lactam class; availability and dosing vary by country.

classes.name: Temocillin
classes.mechanism: Beta-lactam PBP inhibition with stability to many ESBL/AmpC enzymes
classes.spectrum_note: Narrower resistant Enterobacterales-focused agent used mainly in selected regions; lacks Pseudomonas activity.
